a.how: Distinct live article pages of the Articles database that carry at least one reviewer comment - the ARTICLE grain, not the comment grain.
a.query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.page_id) FROM comments c JOIN pages p ON p.id = c.page_id WHERE p.parent_id = '9caee280db7e4c9385908af1164446fb' AND p.in_trash = 0

b.how: notion-search -> notion-fetch -> notion-query-data-sources (the 18 article rows with their Doc stage, has_more false) -> 18 x notion-get-comments with include_all_blocks and include_resolved both true; then count the served articles whose reply carries at least one <comment> element.

gold_derivation.independent_because: b never reads a table. a joins comments/discussions/pages inside the gym's own store through the verifier-only state route; b counts what the SERVED view hands the acting user - the <discussion resolved=...> and <comment> elements inside notion-get-comments' XML, after notion-query-data-sources supplied the 18 page ids from its url column. The two surfaces do not share a query, a join or a table name, so a wrong join in a cannot reach b. They are also the two sides that can genuinely differ here: the tool route reports total-count 0 on every page unless include_all_blocks is set, hides settled threads unless include_resolved is set, and anchors 13 of the 14 threads to a block rather than to the page, none of which the stored table shows.

prompt_claims.claim: Articles are rows of a live database titled Articles - the prompt names both the entity type (a page in a database) and the database's title, so the number of counterexamples it states is 0.
prompt_claims.quote: Every article we publish lives as a page in the Articles database
prompt_claims.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pages p LEFT JOIN databases db ON db.id = p.parent_id WHERE p.parent_id = '9caee280db7e4c9385908af1164446fb' AND (p.parent_type <> 'database_id' OR db.title <> 'Articles' OR db.in_trash <> 0)

prompt_claims.claim: Every reviewer comment on an article belongs to a thread on that same article page - the notes live on the page, not on some other object - so the counterexample count is 0. Note: 13 of the 14 threads are anchored to a block INSIDE the page (context="block"), which is still the page's own comment surface and is why include_all_blocks is needed.
prompt_claims.quote: reviewers leave their notes as comments on the page itself
prompt_claims.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments c JOIN discussions d ON d.id = c.discussion_id JOIN pages p ON p.id = c.page_id WHERE p.parent_id = '9caee280db7e4c9385908af1164446fb' AND d.page_id <> c.page_id

prompt_claims.claim: The prompt gives a thread exactly two states, settled and not settled, and maps them onto the library's resolved flag. The library's reviewer threads take exactly 2 distinct values of that flag, so both states the prompt names really occur.
prompt_claims.quote: A thread somebody has settled is resolved; a thread nobody has settled is still waiting on a person.
prompt_claims.query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT d.resolved) FROM discussions d JOIN pages p ON p.id = d.page_id WHERE p.parent_id = '9caee280db7e4c9385908af1164446fb' AND p.in_trash = 0

prompt_claims.claim: The prompt asserts the article-to-comment fan-out is real, not hypothetical: at least one article carries more than one comment. 1 = at least one such article exists. (Measured here as an existence flag, because the prompt says `may carry`, it states no count.)
prompt_claims.quote: one article (`page id`) may carry several comments
prompt_claims.query: SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END FROM (SELECT c.page_id FROM comments c JOIN pages p ON p.id = c.page_id WHERE p.parent_id = '9caee280db7e4c9385908af1164446fb' AND p.in_trash = 0 GROUP BY c.page_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)

prompt_claims.claim: The prompt asks for a Doc stage on every comment line, which asserts that every article carrying a reviewer comment has a non-empty Doc stage. Counterexamples: 0. (The four articles with no comment have no Doc stage and get no comment line.)
prompt_claims.quote: written as `article title | Doc stage | open`
prompt_claims.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pages p WHERE p.parent_id = '9caee280db7e4c9385908af1164446fb' AND p.in_trash = 0 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM comments c WHERE c.page_id = p.id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM property_values pv JOIN data_source_properties dsp ON dsp.id = pv.property_id AND dsp.name = 'Doc stage' AND dsp.data_source_id = 'ds-9caee280db7e4c9385908af1164446fb' JOIN rich_text_spans rts ON rts.property_value_id = pv.id WHERE pv.page_id = p.id AND TRIM(rts.plain_text) <> '')

prompt_claims.claim: The prompt asserts the two halves of the file exhaust the database: the commented articles plus the uncommented ones are every article in it, with no page counted twice and none left out. Residual stated: 0.
prompt_claims.quote: so that every article in the database appears somewhere in this file
prompt_claims.query: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.page_id) FROM comments c JOIN pages p ON p.id = c.page_id WHERE p.parent_id = '9caee280db7e4c9385908af1164446fb' AND p.in_trash = 0) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pages p WHERE p.parent_id = '9caee280db7e4c9385908af1164446fb' AND p.in_trash = 0 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM comments c WHERE c.page_id = p.id)) - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pages p WHERE p.parent_id = '9caee280db7e4c9385908af1164446fb' AND p.in_trash = 0)

numerals_not_claims_note: instruction.md contains no digit at all and no cardinal number word of two or more (its only number words are the distributive `one` of `one line for every reviewer comment`, `one article`, `one row per metric` and `one title per line`). There is therefore no numeral to exempt, and this list is empty because the prompt states no figure, not because none was checked.
